instruction: I am going on a camping trip with my sisters. I had sent out a checklist of things needed for the trip to them over email. See who has committed to bring what, and place an order on Amazon for the remaining items. Given the available choices pick the highest rated ones.
notes: Information flow: gmail.show_outbox_threads locates the checklist thread; gmail.show_thread reveals the sisters' replies (who committed to what) and the attachment id of the checklist; the attachment is downloaded via gmail.download_attachment (needs a file_system token) and read with file_system.show_file (the evaluation expects file_system.File/Directory changes, so the download is mandatory). The remaining (unclaimed) checklist items are modeled as two placeholder product-type objects (camping-item-1/2) with placeholder queries, quantities and best-product records; the real number of remaining items is determined at runtime by diffing the checklist content against the replies, and the model is instantiated once per remaining item. amazon.search_products is used with sort_by='-rating' so the first result is the highest-rated product; amazon.clear_cart is called first so the order contains only the checklist items (CartEntry changes are ignored by the evaluation). amazon.place_order takes the ordered product types as extra record parameters so that (order-placed) can only become true when every remaining item is in the cart; add-to-cart is blocked after the order is placed, forcing the correct ordering. The task asks no question, so supervisor.complete_task takes no answer.

warnings: domain: pddl-lib parser: types ['object'] of term Variable(c) are not in available types {'payment-card', 'attachment', 'address', 'product', 'quantity', 'token', 'app', 'person', 'password', 'query', 'sort-key', 'file-path', 'product-type', 'username', 'email-thread'}
